newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire government proposes war budget.
newsitem.headline: Zaire government proposes war budget.

text.p: The Zairean government plans to reserve 35 percent of overall public spending in the coming financial year for defence, according to budget proposals submitted to parliament on Friday.

"Just as plans for the state budget had been finished, the launching of the war in the east of the country by Rwanda, Burundi and Uganda, obliged the government to elaborate a war budget," the budget draft, obtained by Reuters, says.
Total projected defence spending for 1997 would be equivalent to $222.43 million, it says.
Parliament met on Friday to debate the budget but the session, which proved heated, was adjourned until Tuesday.
Rwandan-backed rebels have taken over a swathe of territory along Zaire's eastern borders, routing demoralized and poorly equipped Zairean soldiers.
The government has been criticised by the army and radical opposition deputies for having failed to provide the necessary means to defend Zaire.
Government officials say that substantial funds have already been released, but not all the funds have gone beyond the military high command.
Years of corruption and mismanagement in Zaire, combined with international isolation, have drained the state coffers.
In recent weeks, the government has forced local and international businesses to contribute to the war effort with substantial extra taxes each month.
